name: ASIMOV Benchmark v1 + generated robot constitutions
modality: VLM/LLM receives (a) an Imagen-3-edited hazardous version of a real ego-centric home/office frame plus a candidate instruction (ASIMOV-Multimodal), (b) a text injury scenario from hospital reports plus an action (ASIMOV-Injury), (c) an ethical dilemma (ASIMOV-Dilemmas). Scored as binary desirable/undesirable classification accuracy against human-voted labels ('alignment rate'), in normal and adversarial prompting modes.
what_it_measures: Whether a VLM judges robot actions as safe/unsafe the way humans do (semantic safety), and how much auto-generated constitutions raise that alignment versus no-constitution and human-written constitutions.
size: 513,679 contexts / 2,942,060 instructions total (train); validation: Multimodal-Auto 50 contexts/1,311 instr (789 human-labelled), Multimodal-Manual 59/159, Injury 50/319 (163 human-labelled), Dilemmas-Auto 100/200 (35 human-labelled), Dilemmas-SciFi 51/284 (153 human-labelled).
reported_metrics: Top alignment 84.3% (Robot-Constitution128-AutoMerge-AutoAmend10, averaged over normal+adversarial), beating no-constitution and human-written constitutions.
cost_evidence: Generation is automatic (VLM proposes edits, Imagen 3 renders); only ~1,140 validation instructions are human-labelled. No hours, dollars or rater counts stated.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is human voting on desirability; no inter-rater kappa reported; no real-robot or outcome validation. Authors state constitutions are 'for research purposes only, not for deployments requiring safety guarantees'.
notes: Injury subset is text-only (level 0); multimodal subsets are synthetic edited scenes (level 3). CoRL 2025 (PMLR v305). Sizes from Table 1 of the HTML full text.

name: ASIMOV-2.0 (Can AI Perceive Physical Danger and Intervene?)
modality: Three tracks: ASIMOV-2.0-Injury (text NEISS injury narratives, severity/risk QA), ASIMOV-2.0-Constraints (generated image + embodiment-specific constraint text from ISO 10218-1:2025 / ISO/TS 15066 taxonomy; model must say whether an action violates the constraint), ASIMOV-2.0-Video (Veo3-generated clips of safe-to-unsafe transitions; model must flag when intervention is needed). Scored against human-rater consensus labels.
what_it_measures: Risk perception, safety reasoning and intervention triggering of frontier models across text, image and video, including adherence to embodiment-specific operational constraints.
size: Injury 319 annotated scenarios; Video 287 scenarios (severity mix severe 41.5%, moderate 27.7%, mild 12.8%); Constraints 164 (constraint, image) pairs.
reported_metrics: Constraint violation rates 38.6% to 75% across frontier models; no model below 30% when reasoning jointly about embodiment, physics and vision; smaller on-device models 5-20 points lower on risk perception.
cost_evidence: 5 human raters per instance for injury and video; consensus threshold 60% (video) and 80% (constraints). No hours or dollar figures. Videos generated with Veo3.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is multi-rater consensus (no kappa reported). Grounded in real NEISS injury data and ISO constraint taxonomy but no evidence linking scores to real robot incidents.
notes: Injury track is level 0; constraints and video tracks are generated media (level 3). Project page asimov-benchmark.github.io/v2 fetched: data via Colab, no leaderboard numbers on page.

name: BadRobot
modality: Voice/text malicious queries (contextual jailbreak, safety misalignment, conceptual deception) fed to embodied LLM frameworks (VoxPoser, Code-as-Policies, ProgPrompt, VisProg) in simulation and on real arms; outputs scored 1-5 harmfulness by a GPT-4 judge, plus Manipulate Success Rate (MSR).
what_it_measures: How easily an LLM-driven manipulator can be induced to plan and execute physically harmful, illegal or privacy-violating actions.
size: 277 malicious queries across 7 categories; 77 VoxPoser subtasks from RLBench; real-world: 35 evaluations per attack on UR3e and myCobot 280-Pi.
reported_metrics: MSR up to 83% (contextual jailbreak, GPT-4-turbo), 75% (safety misalignment, GPT-3.5), 74% (conceptual deception, Yi-vision); real-world average MSR 68.57% vs 22.85% baseline.
cost_evidence: Two low-cost arms (UR3e, myCobot 280-Pi); 35 real trials per attack; no hours/dollars stated; notes 'expert-level physical access' as a misuse barrier.
validity_evidence: Harmfulness scored by GPT-4 judge; no human-judge agreement reported. Real-robot executions confirm plans translate to motion but no injury outcome data.
notes: ICLR 2025. Numbers from HTML full text (v4/v5).

name: SafeAgentBench
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Shanghai AI Lab
modality: Embodied LLM agent (9 planner baselines) receives a natural-language household task in SafeAgentEnv (AI2-THOR v5.0, 17 high-level actions); scored by (i) execution: does the plan run and satisfy goal conditions, (ii) semantic: GPT-4o judge on whether the plan is safe/complete; rejection rate of hazardous tasks.
what_it_measures: Whether LLM task planners recognise and refuse explicitly and implicitly hazardous household tasks while still completing safe ones.
size: 750 tasks (450 detailed unsafe, 100 abstract unsafe, 200 safe) over 10 hazard types and 3 task types; 9 baselines.
reported_metrics: Best baseline rejects only 10% of detailed hazardous tasks; 32% of abstract ones; <3% spread in proactive-defense rate across LLMs; KARMA 70% safe completion on long-horizon.
cost_evidence: Mostly CPU experiments; one RTX 4090 for open models via vLLM. Human review of all instructions and goal conditions; annotator count not stated.
validity_evidence: GPT-4o judge vs human consistency 91.89% / 90.36% / 90.70% on the three task types from a 1,008-rating user study. No real-robot validation.
notes: One of the few entries reporting judge-vs-human agreement. v5 Oct 2025.

name: IS-Bench
modality: VLM-driven agent acts in OmniGibson household scenes from egocentric observations; process-oriented evaluation checks that risk-mitigation actions occur before/after specific risk-prone steps. Metrics: Success Rate, Safe Success Rate, Safety Recall, Safety Awareness.
what_it_measures: Interactive safety: whether an embodied VLM agent perceives emergent risks during execution and orders mitigation steps correctly, not just post-hoc plan safety.
size: 161 scenarios, 388 unique safety risks, 10 domestic safety categories; risks 24.2% pre-caution / 75.8% post-caution.
reported_metrics: GPT-4o SR 81.3% but SSR 33.8%; safety-aware CoT +9.3% safety but -9.4% task success.
cost_evidence: One A100 80GB; each evaluation session 2.5-3 h depending on VLM inference time. Every reference plan manually executed and verified by human annotators in the simulator.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is human-verified executable plans; no inter-annotator statistics; no real-world transfer evidence.
notes: AAAI 2026. Rare explicit wall-clock cost statement.

name: ForesightSafety-VLA
org: BrainCog Lab, Chinese Academy of Sciences (Yi Zeng)
modality: VLA policies run closed-loop in RoboTwin (5 embodiments) on safety-augmented scenarios varied along scene structure, language command (W0-W4 templates) and visual observation; scored by cumulative safety cost (CC), risk exposure time (RET), and a four-quadrant safe/unsafe x success/failure decomposition.
what_it_measures: Process-level physical, instruction-side and perception-side safety of VLA policies under a 13-category taxonomy (Safe-Core, Safe-Lang, Safe-Vis).
size: 66 base scenarios; 50 episodes x 3 seeds per model-task-setting; 4 fully evaluated baselines (OpenVLA-OFT, RDT, Diffusion Policy, ACT) plus partial runs of pi0.5, pi0, DexVLA, LLaVA-VLA, TinyVLA, DP3.
reported_metrics: CC 0.18 (OpenVLA-OFT) to 0.39 (ACT); unsafe share of successful episodes 12.5% (OpenVLA-OFT), 25.0% (RDT), 29.4% (DP), 37.5% (ACT). Structure and visual variation degrade safety more than language variation.
cost_evidence: Language templates W0-W2 human-authored, W3-W4 LLM-generated then manually verified; no compute or wall-clock stated.
validity_evidence: Simulator-computed safety predicates; no human agreement study, no real-robot validation.
notes: v2 June 2026.

name: SafePlan (+ SafePlan benchmark)
modality: Natural-language task prompts (safe or unsafe) fed to an LLM planner wrapped with Prompt-Sanity, Invariant, Precondition and Postcondition chain-of-thought reasoners; scored as accept/reject confusion matrix against expert safe/unsafe labels; plans exercised in AI2-THOR.
what_it_measures: Ability of an LLM robotic task planner to reject harmful task prompts while accepting safe ones.
size: 621 expert-curated prompts (127 safe, 494 unsafe) across assistive, navigation, manipulation domains and 3 complexity levels.
reported_metrics: 90.5% reduction in harmful-prompt acceptance; Gemini 1.5 Pro unsafe acceptance 61.34% -> 7.09%, accuracy 88.4%, safe acceptance 70.9%.
cost_evidence: Expert curation of 621 prompts; annotator count not stated; no compute or latency figures.
validity_evidence: Labels are expert judgement; no inter-rater statistics; no real-robot experiments.
notes: Prompt classification is text-only (level 0); AI2-THOR used for plan execution only. Follow-up SafeGate (obi2026safegate) adds real-robot tests.

name: RoboGuard
modality: Two-stage guardrail: root-of-trust LLM grounds safety rules into temporal-logic specs from the scene graph; control synthesis rejects/repairs unsafe LLM plans. Evaluated with RoboPAIR-style jailbreak prompts on a Clearpath Jackal in simulation (indoor/outdoor, ~20,000 m^2) and real world; metric is attack success rate (ASR).
what_it_measures: Reduction in executed unsafe plans under worst-case jailbreaks without loss of safe-plan performance.
size: 70 adversarial prompts (7 harmful behaviours x 10 rephrasings) + 10 safe behaviours; >1,500 evaluations across attack variants.
reported_metrics: Unguarded ASR 92.3% +/- 4.7%; with RoboGuard <3%; uses 12-21% of attacker tokens and 1 LLM query vs attacker's 15.
cost_evidence: Onboard compute Nvidia A4000 + Ryzen 5 3600 on the Jackal; token and query counts reported; no hours stated.
validity_evidence: ASR is judged by whether the robot executes the target behaviour; no human-agreement study; controlled-lab real robot only.
notes: IEEE RA-L accepted Feb 2026; v2 March 2026. Code: github.com/KumarRobotics/RoboGuard.

name: RoboPAIR (Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots)
modality: Attacker LLM iteratively rewrites prompts (K=10 iterations) until the target LLM-controlled robot emits a harmful executable plan; three settings: white-box NVIDIA Dolphins driving LLM, gray-box Clearpath Jackal + GPT-4o, black-box Unitree Go2 + GPT-3.5. Success judged by execution of the target action, checked by two expert human annotators.
what_it_measures: Attack success rate for eliciting physically harmful robot actions from LLM planners across access levels.
size: 3 datasets x 7 harmful actions x 5 trials = 35 attempts per robot.
reported_metrics: RoboPAIR 35/35 on all three robots (100%); baselines also high; first jailbreak of a deployed commercial robot (Go2).
cost_evidence: Max 10 queries per harmful action; two expert annotators verify each jailbreak; no dollars/hours stated.
validity_evidence: Human-verified successes (2 experts, no kappa); lab-only, no injury outcomes.
notes: Project page robopair.org. Dolphins setting is text/video QA (level 0-2); Go2/Jackal are level 7.

name: Embodied Red Teaming (ERT)
modality: VLM generates diverse, contextually grounded paraphrased instructions for language-conditioned policies (3D-Diffuser, GR-1, OpenVLA) in CALVIN, RLBench and SimplerEnv; scored by task success rate drop; unsafe behaviour (objects knocked off table) shown qualitatively.
what_it_measures: Robustness of language-conditioned robot policies to instruction phrasing and whether benchmark instruction sets overstate performance.
size: CALVIN 10 instr x 27 tasks = 270 (3 refinement rounds); RLBench 3-6 instr x 18 tasks; SimplerEnv 4 instr x 25 initial states.
reported_metrics: 3D-Diffuser CALVIN 90% -> 53%, RLBench 79% -> 3%; OpenVLA SimplerEnv 76.0% -> 30.8 +/- 3.8%.
cost_evidence: None stated; fully automated instruction generation.
validity_evidence: No human study; safety scored qualitatively only.
notes: safety_focus false because the quantitative metric is task success; safety is a qualitative side observation.

name: MSSBench (Multimodal Situational Safety)
modality: MLLM receives an image (safe or unsafe situation) plus a language query; must respond safely (chat) or refuse/adapt an action (embodied, images from embodied simulators). GPT-4o judge classifies responses as safe/unsafe; accuracy on unsafe vs safe halves.
what_it_measures: Whether a VLM's safety judgement depends correctly on the visual situation rather than the query alone.
size: 1,820 query-image pairs (half safe, half unsafe); 760 pairs in the embodied subset; 4 domains, 10 categories.
reported_metrics: Best embodied accuracy ~59% (Claude: 55.9% on unsafe, 98.4% on safe); models misclassify unsafe embodied situations; captions improve results (visual understanding is bottleneck).
cost_evidence: Manual authoring of unsafe household tasks and situations; no annotator counts or hours.
validity_evidence: GPT-4o judge; no judge-vs-human agreement reported; no real-world validation.
notes: ICLR 2025.

name: LLM-Driven Robots Risk Enacting Discrimination, Violence, and Unlawful Actions
org: Carnegie Mellon / King's College London / University of Birmingham
modality: Text prompts describing HRI scenarios (facial expression, proxemics, security, rescue, task assignment) with protected-identity descriptors, plus open-vocabulary dangerous instructions, sent to several LLMs; outputs coded for discriminatory outcomes and acceptance of harmful/unlawful commands.
what_it_measures: Whether LLMs used as robot decision-makers produce discriminatory or unsafe action choices across protected characteristics and accept dangerous open-vocabulary instructions.
size: Not quantified in abstract; several LLMs; code released on GitHub.
reported_metrics: Models produced directly discriminatory outcomes and accepted dangerous instructions (e.g., removing mobility aids, sexual predation).
validity_evidence: Author-coded harms; no inter-rater statistics; no physical robot experiments.
notes: International Journal of Social Robotics 2025.

name: EARBench (EAIRiskBench)
modality: Multi-agent pipeline: foundation models generate safety guidelines, risk-prone scene descriptions (text or image), a target model plans the task, and an automated evaluator scores the plan; Task Risk Rate (TRR) = fraction of plans exhibiting hazardous behaviour.
what_it_measures: Physical-risk awareness of foundation-model task planners in generated risk-prone scenes.
size: EARDataset 2,636 samples (1,318 textual + 1,318 visual) over 28 scenes and 7 domains.
reported_metrics: Average TRR 95.75%; GPT-4o 94.03%, Claude 3 95.05%, Gemini 1.5 Flash 93.67%.
cost_evidence: Fully automated generation and judging; no compute or annotation cost stated.
validity_evidence: Judge-vs-human Cohen's kappa ~0.48 without safety tips, ~0.85 with safety tips provided to the judge.
notes: Half the set is text-only (level 0), half visual (level 1). Kappa figures from HTML v5.

name: SafeVLA + Safety-CHORES
modality: VLA policy trained/evaluated in AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR (150K scenes, 800K Objaverse assets) on Safety-ObjNav, Safety-PickUp, Safety-Fetch with five constraint families (corners, blind spots, fragile collections, critical points, dangerous equipment); cost 1 per violating step; metrics cumulative cost and success rate.
what_it_measures: Safety-performance trade-off of VLA policies under fine-grained physical constraints in long-horizon mobile manipulation.
size: Procedural scenes (150K); 3 task families; training 15M-25M steps.
reported_metrics: 83.58% reduction in cumulative safety cost vs SOTA with +3.85% success.
cost_evidence: RL training budget 15M-25M environment steps per task; no hours/dollars.
validity_evidence: Simulator-defined costs; limited sim-to-real demonstration on a dual-arm platform; no human agreement study.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 spotlight.

name: SciFi-Benchmark
modality: LLM answers multiple-choice decision questions extracted from 824 sci-fi works (LLM introspection generates situations, decisions and alternatives); scored as alignment with human-voted answers, with and without constitutions.
what_it_measures: Value alignment of LLM decisions in robot-relevant dilemmas and the effect of generated constitutions.
size: 9,056 questions / 53,384 answers generated; human-labelled eval set (284 instructions, 153 human-labelled per ASIMOV Table 1).
reported_metrics: Alignment 79.4% -> 95.8% with generated constitutions; sci-fi 'unsettling' decisions align 21.2%.
cost_evidence: Automatic generation; small human-voted eval set; no hours.
validity_evidence: Human voting ground truth; no kappa; no physical validation.
notes: v2 July 2025.

name: SafeMind / SafeMindBench
org: BrainCog Lab, Chinese Academy of Sciences
modality: Image (DALL-E 3 rendered) + instruction pairs across Instr-Risk, Env-Risk, Order-Fix, Req-Align; agent outputs an action sequence validated against a skill set, then a GPT-4 judge checks constraints. Metrics: Safety Rate, Success Rate, Effectiveness Rate.
what_it_measures: Safety of embodied LLM agents across task understanding, environment perception and action ordering under sabotage/harm/privacy/illegal scenarios.
reported_metrics: GPT-4o safety rate 10.3% (Instr-Risk), 19.1% (Env-Risk), 61.1% (Order-Fix), 89.7% (Req-Align), weighted 37.2%.
cost_evidence: LLM-synthesis-human-verification pipeline; annotator counts and cost not stated.
validity_evidence: GPT-4 judge; no judge-vs-human agreement; no real robot.

name: SafeRelBench
modality: VLM-driven agent executes household tasks whose safety depends on spatial relations; process-level safety compliance tracked separately from task success; 248 spatial-relation samples vs 259 non-spatial controls.
what_it_measures: Whether embodied VLM agents respect spatial-relation-dependent safety constraints during execution.
size: 507 executable samples (248 spatial, 259 control); 7 VLM agents.
reported_metrics: Agents frequently complete tasks while violating process-level safety constraints (numbers not in abstract).
notes: Simulator not named in abstract; level 4 assumed from 'executable' samples.

name: EgoSafetyBench
modality: Synthetic egocentric robot-view videos (Kling v3 text-to-video) annotated at 0.5 s granularity; VLM acts as streaming guard and must flag hazards; contrastive ladders differ by a single deciding cue. Metrics: chunk-level hazard recall, false-alarm rate on safe content, timely detection within 0.5 s.
what_it_measures: Runtime hazard detection and over-intervention of VLMs on temporally evolving egocentric scenes.
reported_metrics: Claude-Sonnet-4.6: ~79% chunk-level hazard recall, 17.3% false alarms on safe content, 57.4% timely detection; Gemini-3.5-Flash false alarms rise 16.0% -> 36.6% with misleading signs; weak models miss up to a third of hazards.
cost_evidence: Two annotators per video plus third resolver; no hours/dollars; videos generated not filmed.
validity_evidence: Inter-annotator agreement 91.2% (kappa 0.744) chunk-level, 90.5% (kappa 0.804) video-level. No real-footage or outcome validation.
notes: Best-documented inter-annotator agreement in the catalogue; reports both sensitivity and false-alarm behaviour.

name: SafeVLA-Bench
modality: VLA rollouts in LIBERO and RoboCasa-365 monitored by Signal Temporal Logic specs (excessive contact, bystander disturbance, held-object destabilisation, self-contact); reports Succ-But-Unsafe (SBU) and Violation Severity Index (VSI) alongside native success.
what_it_measures: The success-safety gap: how often nominally successful VLA episodes violate physical safety requirements.
reported_metrics: 13-15% unsafe-episode rates for tabletop baselines; 36-56% of successful RoboCasa-365 rollouts violate requirements.
validity_evidence: Simulator predicates only; no human or real-world validation.

name: LIBERO-Safety
modality: Parametric safety benchmark on LIBERO with procedurally generated physical and semantic hazards; 8 VLAs and 2 embodied foundation models evaluated; keypose-driven pipeline yields collision-free demonstrations for training.
what_it_measures: Physical and semantic safety of VLA policies and the effect of training-data diversity on safe trajectories.
reported_metrics: High-diversity training fosters safer trajectories; bottlenecks from trajectory synthesis and semantic misalignment (numbers not in abstract).
cost_evidence: Human teleoperation used for part of data collection; no hours stated.
notes: ECCV 2026 per abstract page.

name: HazardArena
modality: Safe/unsafe twin scenarios with matched objects and layouts but different semantic risk; VLA executes in physics simulation; stage-wise predicates (attempt, commit, success) computed automatically; on unsafe twins 'success' equals hazard completion.
what_it_measures: Whether VLAs recognise when an otherwise valid action becomes hazardous, isolating safety judgement from motor skill.
size: >2,000 assets, 40-51 risk-sensitive tasks (v1 says 40, v3 abstract says 51), 7 hazard families; 4 VLA backbones.
reported_metrics: pi0: 0.47 success on safe 'insert outlet' vs 0.44 on unsafe twin (little refusal); safe-only fine-tuning raises hazardous execution on unsafe twins.
validity_evidence: v3 abstract claims physical-world experiments confirm transfer; v1 full text reported simulation only. No human study.
notes: Version drift between v1 and v3 on task count and real-world claims; cite v3.

name: ResponsibleRobotBench
modality: MLLM agent plans multi-stage manipulation in a physics simulator with electrical, chemical and human-related hazards; may request human assistance (cost 10,000 units vs 100 per action); automatic safety rate, success rate, safe success rate.
what_it_measures: Responsible manipulation: completing tasks while avoiding hazards and escalating to humans when needed.
reported_metrics: GPT-4o: safety 0.72, success 0.82, safe-success 0.64; fire/chemical safety only 0.46.
cost_evidence: Explicit cost model inside the benchmark (human intervention = 100x an action) but no real evaluation cost stated.
validity_evidence: Simulator predicates; no human or real-robot validation (title claims sim-to-real framework, experiments are sim).

name: Safe-BeAl / SafePlan-Bench
org: University of Science and Technology of China
modality: LLM agent plans household tasks in VirtualHome; a rule-based detector maps actions/states to 88 hazard categories (no LLM judge); safety rate and task success reported.
what_it_measures: Task-planning safety of LLM embodied agents over 8 hazard categories and the gain from Safe-Align fine-tuning.
size: 2,027 daily tasks with environments (SafeRisks), 8 hazard categories.
reported_metrics: GPT-4 few-shot 82.49% safe; Llama-3.1-8B + Safe-Align 86.38%; Safe-BeAl improves safety 8.55-15.22% over GPT-4-based agents.
cost_evidence: Tasks LLM-generated from manually found hazard seeds then manually filtered; no hours.
validity_evidence: Rule-based detector avoids judge noise but its agreement with human judgement is not quantified.

name: SAFER (Safety Aware Task Planning)
modality: Multi-LLM planner with a Safety Agent critic and control barrier functions; safety violations quantified by an LLM-as-a-Judge metric; hardware experiments with multiple heterogeneous robots and a human.
what_it_measures: Reduction of safety violations in long-horizon multi-robot LLM planning.
reported_metrics: Fewer violations than SOTA LLM planners at similar efficiency (numbers not in abstract).
cost_evidence: Hardware experiments with multiple robots; no counts or hours.
validity_evidence: LLM-as-a-Judge safety metric with no reported human agreement.
notes: Human present in hardware tests but no field/at-risk protocol described.

name: SPOC
modality: LLM plans step-by-step under strict partial observability and physical constraints in a symbolic household environment; goal-condition-based evaluation with state- and constraint-based online metrics.
what_it_measures: Safety-aware planning under implicit constraints (fire, fluid, injury, damage, pollution).
reported_metrics: SOTA LLMs struggle, especially under implicit constraints.
notes: ICASSP 2026. Symbolic environment, no perception, hence level 0.

name: Modular Safety Guardrails Are Necessary (position)
org: Purdue / Texas A&M / NVIDIA and others
modality: No evaluation; argues for action, decision and human-centred safety layers with monitoring and intervention modules.
what_it_measures: Argues static verification, monolithic controllers and end-to-end policies are insufficient for FM-enabled robots.
reported_metrics: n/a

name: From Refusal to Recovery (control-theoretic guardrails)
modality: Safety-critical RL learns a predictive guardrail that monitors an LLM agent's proposed actions and steers them to safe ones; evaluated in simulated driving and e-commerce.
what_it_measures: Whether predictive, recovery-based guardrails avoid catastrophic outcomes (collision, bankruptcy) while preserving task performance, versus flag-and-block refusal.
reported_metrics: Guardrails prevent catastrophic outcomes in both domains (no numbers in abstract).
notes: IASEAI 2026. Key reused from speaker-bajcsy.json.

name: HomeSafeBench
org: Beijing Institute of Technology and collaborators
modality: Embodied VLM freely explores a VirtualHome scene from first-person view and must report hazards across five categories; scored by F1 against human-validated hazard lists.
what_it_measures: Active home-safety inspection: finding hazards through exploration rather than answering about a fixed image.
reported_metrics: Best model 34.7% F1 vs 98.0% human F1; CueBack fine-tuning 18.7% -> 45.3% F1 on OOD test.
cost_evidence: Human validation of tasks; human-inspector baseline run; no hours.
validity_evidence: Human ceiling measured (98.0% F1) which bounds label noise; no real-home validation.
notes: Distinct from HomeSafe-Bench (pu2026homesafebench).

name: HomeSafe-Bench (unsafe action detection)
modality: Videos built from physical simulation plus video generation depicting embodied-agent actions; VLM must detect unsafe behaviour and temporally localise the hazard; HD-Guard hierarchical monitor proposed.
what_it_measures: Detection and temporal localisation of embodied-agent-specific unsafe actions in household video.
reported_metrics: Bottlenecks in VLM-based safety detection identified; HD-Guard gives better latency-performance trade-off (numbers not in abstract).

name: GuardianBench
modality: Same-scene safe/unsafe instruction pairs; VLM must judge each; pair accuracy requires both members correct; construction grounded in safety standards.
what_it_measures: Latent contextual risk recognition: distinguishing safe from unsafe instructions given identical scenes.
reported_metrics: Average pair accuracy only 24.1% for primary models.

name: RoboJailBench
modality: Unified harness with 4 attacks, 2 defenses, 5 augmented datasets with paired adversarial/benign goals, 18 consequence categories; measures security and utility trade-off; public leaderboard.
what_it_measures: Comparative attack/defense evaluation for VLM-based embodied agents with a security-vs-utility trade-off.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.
notes: Platform (sim vs real) not stated; level 1 assumed for VLM-level evaluation.

name: EmbodiedGovBench
modality: Scenario templates and perturbation operators applied to embodied capability runtimes; seven governance metrics (unauthorised capability invocation, drift robustness, recovery, policy portability, upgrade safety, human override responsiveness, audit completeness).
what_it_measures: Governability of embodied agent systems and fleets rather than per-episode safety.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.
notes: Level left null: abstract does not say what environment the runtimes execute in.

name: Semantic Anomaly Detection with LLMs
modality: Scene descriptions from an autonomous-driving FSM policy and a learned manipulation policy are given to an LLM monitor that flags semantic anomalies; compared with human reasoning on the same cases.
what_it_measures: Whether an LLM can serve as a runtime monitor for semantically anomalous, policy-confusing situations.
reported_metrics: Reported 'agreement with human reasoning' (qualitative in abstract).
validity_evidence: Compared against human judgement; no kappa; no deployment data.
notes: Autonomous Robots 2023 (journal version). Precursor to AESOP.

name: AESOP (Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Reactive Planning with LLMs)
modality: Fast binary anomaly classifier in LLM embedding space triggers slow generative-LLM fallback selection; MPC keeps the robot safe during LLM latency; 500 randomised quadrotor simulations plus physical drone experiments.
what_it_measures: Runtime detection of semantic out-of-distribution failures and safe recovery under latency and compute constraints.
size: 500 randomised simulation scenarios; hardware quadrotor demos.
reported_metrics: 100% recovery in simulation vs 77-85% crash/failure for latency-ignoring baselines (per project summary); fast classifier beats autoregressive GPT reasoning even with small LMs.
cost_evidence: Explicit latency budget analysis; no dollars or hours.
validity_evidence: Hardware confirmation of recovery; no human-agreement or field data.
notes: RSS 2024. The 100%/77-85% figures come from a search summary, not the abstract; treat as medium.

name: Encoding Inequity (LLM caregiving bias)
modality: Caregiving prompts with demographic descriptors sent to an LLM; responses analysed by sentiment and narrative clustering.
what_it_measures: Demographic bias in LLM-generated robot caregiving behaviour.
reported_metrics: Reduced sentiment for disability and LGBTQ+ identities; stereotyped clustering.
notes: HRI 2025 DEI workshop. Fairness rather than physical safety.

name: RoboInspector
modality: User instructions at varying granularity for two LLM policy-code frameworks; generated code executed in simulation and on a real arm; failures categorised into four unreliable-behaviour classes; failure-feedback refinement.
what_it_measures: Reliability (not explicitly safety) of LLM-generated robot policy code across task complexity and instruction granularity.
reported_metrics: Refinement improves policy-code reliability by up to 35%.
notes: ACM TIST. safety_focus false: reliability framing.

name: Communication Attacks in LLM-Controlled Multi-Robot Systems
modality: External entry-point and privileged in-system message injection into three multi-agent architectures (DMAS, HMAS-1, HMAS-2) across 3 LLMs and 5 embodied multi-robot tasks; unsafe action success rates measured; CPV gate mitigation.
what_it_measures: Vulnerability of LLM multi-robot coordination to injected messages.
reported_metrics: DMAS 96.7% entry endorsement, 100% activation; HMAS-1 97.8% unsafe action success; HMAS-2 88.3% unsafe slots; mitigation 70.0% -> 36.6%.
notes: Simulation platform not stated in abstract, level left null.

name: VLA Safety survey (Threats, Challenges, Evaluations, Mechanisms)
modality: Survey organised by training-time vs inference-time threats, defenses, evaluations and deployment.
what_it_measures: Maps VLA attack/defense/evaluation literature; flags lack of standardised evaluation and certified robustness for embodied trajectories.
reported_metrics: n/a
notes: v2 Aug 2026.

name: Gemini Robotics tech report (ASIMOV safety eval section)
modality: Gemini Robotics-ER evaluated on ASIMOV-Multimodal and ASIMOV-Injury (image/text + instruction, human-labelled desirability) with and without constitutions; bias-inducing pointing queries scored by rejection rate.
what_it_measures: Semantic action safety of a deployed robotics foundation model, measured offline with ASIMOV.
reported_metrics: 96% rejection of bias-inducing pointing queries vs 20% baseline; ASIMOV results shown in Fig. 29 without numbers in text.
validity_evidence: Report explicitly scopes to semantic safety; no collision/force testing numbers for Gemini Robotics-ER.
notes: 118+ authors; key reused from speaker-sindhwani.json.

name: Evaluating Gemini Robotics Policies in a Veo World Simulator
modality: Action-conditioned Veo video model used as a generative simulator; policy rollouts scored by human binary success; nominal, OOD (background, distractors, objects) and red-teaming safety probes (edited scenes with hazards, ambiguity); compared to 1,600+ real-robot evaluations.
what_it_measures: Whether a generative world simulator predicts real-world policy success and can surface physical/semantic safety failures cheaply.
reported_metrics: OOD single-policy: Pearson 0.86 predicted vs real success, MMRV 0.06; strong nominal linear correlation (Fig. 4).
cost_evidence: 1,600+ real trials used as ground truth; human scoring of every episode; no hours/dollars stated.
validity_evidence: Strongest sim-vs-real validity evidence in the catalogue for a generative simulator; no inter-rater stats.
notes: Key reused from speaker-sindhwani.json (which placed it at level 6; task ladder places generative photoreal simulation at 5).

name: Predictive Red Teaming (RoboART)
modality: Generative image editing perturbs policy observations along 12 off-nominal factors (lighting, distractors, object locations); a policy-specific anomaly detector predicts success-rate degradation; validated against hardware trials.
what_it_measures: Whether cheap synthetic perturbations predict real-robot performance drops without running the robot.
reported_metrics: Mean absolute gap between predicted and real success rate <0.19; fine-tuning on adversarial-condition data boosts baseline 2-7x.
cost_evidence: 500+ hardware trials for validation; the proxy itself needs no robot time.
validity_evidence: Direct predicted-vs-real comparison on hardware (the sibling speaker file reports Spearman 0.8).
notes: safety_focus false: targets task-success robustness, not hazard behaviour, but is the cleanest proxy-validity study.

name: VLESA
modality: Egocentric frames with goal-conditioned safety annotations; GRPO-trained safety Q-filter plus intent-action predictor; evaluated on ASIMOV-2.0 intervention-frame accuracy.
what_it_measures: Real-time intervention triggering from egocentric video of human activity.
reported_metrics: Q-filter improves action safety >41 points; higher exact-frame intervention accuracy than baselines.

name: Hazard or Anomaly? (VLM danger vs discrepancy)
modality: Scene images labelled hazardous vs merely anomalous; VLMs prompted under several strategies; tests whether the distinction changes model behaviour.
what_it_measures: Whether VLMs conflate unusualness with danger (false-alarm behaviour).
size: Two datasets; public set on Roboflow; size not in abstract.
reported_metrics: VLMs frequently misinterpret anomalousness as hazardousness.
notes: RO-MAN 2026.

name: InspecSafe-V1 (industrial inspection safety)
modality: Real multi-sensor records (RGB, IR video, audio, depth and radar point clouds, gas, temperature, humidity) from routine operations of inspection robots, each with a scene description and safety-level label; pixel-level segmentation for key objects.
what_it_measures: Multimodal safety-level assessment in real industrial inspection scenes.
size: 5,013 instances from 41 robots at 2,239 sites, 5 industrial scenarios, 7 modalities.
reported_metrics: Dataset paper; no model numbers in abstract.
cost_evidence: Data collected during routine operations (operational cost absorbed); manual segmentation annotation.
validity_evidence: Labels are practitioner safety levels; no inter-annotator statistics in abstract.
notes: Scientific Data (accepted). Real operational data replayed offline: level 5.

name: AttackVLA / BackdoorVLA
modality: Unified framework across data construction, training and inference; implements existing VLA attacks and adapted VLM attacks; BackdoorVLA forces attacker-specified long-horizon action sequences on trigger; sim benchmarks and real robot.
what_it_measures: Targeted attack success against VLAs across the development lifecycle.
reported_metrics: BackdoorVLA average targeted success 58.4%, 100% on selected tasks.

name: Adversarial Attacks on Robotic VLAs (RoboGCG)
modality: LLM jailbreak-style textual attacks applied once at rollout start to billion-parameter VLAs; measures reachability of the full action space and persistence over horizon.
what_it_measures: Whether text-only attacks give full control authority over VLA action space.
reported_metrics: Textual attacks give full reachability of action space and persist over long horizons.
notes: Simulation setting not detailed in abstract.

name: Adversarial patches against VLAs
org: Rochester Institute of Technology and collaborators
modality: Small colourful adversarial patch in the camera view; success-rate reduction across simulated robotic tasks; physical deployment capability claimed.
what_it_measures: Vulnerability of VLA control to visual patch attacks.
reported_metrics: Up to 100% reduction in task success.
notes: ICCV 2025.

name: Robots Enact Malignant Stereotypes
org: Johns Hopkins / Georgia Tech / University of Washington
modality: CLIP-based robot manipulation methods in simulation given blocks bearing faces varying by race and gender plus stereotyped commands (e.g., 'pack the criminal'); action selection frequencies compared to uniform.
what_it_measures: Whether pretrained vision-language robot policies act out gender/race stereotypes and physiognomy.
reported_metrics: Robots acted out toxic stereotypes at scale; less likely to recognise women and people of colour.
notes: FAccT 2022 (ACM DOI 10.1145/3531146.3533138; ACM page returned 403, arXiv page fetched).

name: FreezeVLA
modality: Min-max bi-level optimisation produces adversarial images that make VLAs ignore subsequent instructions (action freezing); tested on 3 VLAs over 4 robotic benchmarks.
what_it_measures: Availability-style attacks that stall robot action.
reported_metrics: 76.2% average attack success; transferable across prompts.

name: LIBERO-VIFO
modality: Visual cues (8 families) placed in LIBERO scenes; Part I tests authorised cue following, Part II unauthorised cue following under language-cue conflict and empty language; 7 VLAs; extended to safety-critical settings and real robot.
what_it_measures: Whether VLAs execute tasks indicated by unauthorised visual cues (a prompt-injection-like risk).
reported_metrics: Models execute cue-indicated tasks without language instruction (numbers not in abstract).
validity_evidence: Real-robot deployment reported; no human study.

name: ShieldVLA
modality: HJ-reachability safety critic learned from images; rubric-based VLM safety scores replace manual cost labels; evaluated on 5 navigation/manipulation benchmarks.
what_it_measures: Safety-cost reduction of VLAs via feasibility-aware alignment.
reported_metrics: 57% average cumulative safety cost reduction; +0.13 success vs SafeVLA.
cost_evidence: Avoids manual cost annotation by using VLM rubric scores (cost-motivated design).

name: Safe Embodied AI for Long-horizon Tasks (cross-layer survey)
modality: Survey by intervention timing (planning-, policy-, execution-time); grades evidence as formal, statistical or heuristic.
what_it_measures: Identifies weak evidence for policy-time safety and a lack of manipulation-specific safety benchmarks.
reported_metrics: n/a

name: ROBOSHACKLES
org: University of Science and Technology of China
modality: Real DROID observations edited into hazardous states with temporal prompts; embodied foundation models must refuse; unsafe action generation rate under a refusal criterion; 2 direct-harm and 4 indirect-harm categories.
what_it_measures: Whether embodied foundation models refuse actions that would injure humans in edited real scenes.
reported_metrics: 100% unsafe action generation rate across all six EFMs tested.
cost_evidence: Automated pipeline from DROID; none stated.
notes: v2 Aug 2026.

name: REALM (red-teaming physical-world VLMs)
modality: 12 red-teaming methods, 3 defenses, 13 VLMs under a unified protocol; agentic pipeline generates physically grounded attack objectives.
what_it_measures: Comparative attack effectiveness against VLMs used for physical-world tasks.
reported_metrics: Text/typographic injection causes most failures; single-pass attacks near iterative ones at lower cost; scale does not confer robustness.

name: SafeStage
modality: 97 risk scenarios across pre-, during- and post-manipulation stages; event- and state-based checks; native success reported separately from stage-specific safety.
what_it_measures: Stage-resolved safety failure profiles of VLA and world-model policies.
reported_metrics: Nominal completion frequently coexists with violations (numbers not in abstract).
notes: Environment not stated; level 4 assumed from event/state checks.

name: MANIGUARD
modality: LTLf automaton monitors over physics predicates score foundation-model manipulation policies on 200 locked base tasks (1,000 scenarios with shifts) in simulation and on a physical Franka; 8,000 safety-annotated demos (40 per task) for improvement.
what_it_measures: Specification-grounded safety of manipulation policies, independent of task success.
size: 200 base tasks, 1,000 scenarios, 8,000 demos, 6 task families.
reported_metrics: 6-21% of successful rollouts violate the specification; fine-tuning raises safe completion to 7.5-29.8%.
cost_evidence: 8,000 demos via motion planning plus human teleoperation; no hours stated.
validity_evidence: Automated monitors rather than learned judges; physical Franka evaluation; no human-agreement study.

name: OopsieVerse / DamageSim
modality: DamageSim converts contact forces, temperature changes and liquid interactions into explicit damage signals in OmniGibson and RoboCasa; used to evaluate IL, RL and VLA policies.
what_it_measures: Physically grounded, task-agnostic damage measurement for manipulation/navigation policies.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.

name: When Robots Mishear Us (ASR errors and embodied safety)
modality: Simulated ASR errors injected into SafeAgentBench and POEX instructions; measures whether errors preserve semantics, add harmful ambiguity or weaken refusals; tests automatic error correction.
what_it_measures: Effect of speech-recognition noise on acceptance of harmful instructions by embodied LLM agents.
reported_metrics: ASR errors cause harmful instructions to be accepted/executed; correction only partly effective.

name: POEX / Harmful-RLbench
modality: Hidden-layer gradient optimisation produces harmful yet executable policy code; multi-agent evaluator judges jailbroken policies; Harmful-RLbench of human-object-environment risks; simulation and real robots.
what_it_measures: Policy-executable jailbreak success against LLM-based robots (executability as a distinct requirement).
reported_metrics: Not in abstract; shows text-only jailbreaks are inapplicable to robots.
validity_evidence: Multi-agent evaluator; no human agreement in abstract.
notes: v3 Aug 2025.

name: Q-DIG (quality-diversity red teaming of VLAs)
modality: Quality-diversity search with VLMs generates diverse adversarial instructions for VLAs across simulation benchmarks; real-world checks of generated prompts.
what_it_measures: Instruction-space fragility of VLAs and fine-tuning gains from adversarial prompts.
reported_metrics: Real-world evaluations consistent with simulation (no numbers in abstract).
notes: safety_focus false: robustness/task success.

name: Blindfold (action-level jailbreak)
modality: Adversarial proxy planning yields action sequences that look semantically safe but cause harmful physical effects; tested in embodied simulators and on a real 6-DoF arm.
what_it_measures: Attack success for semantically disguised harmful action plans.
reported_metrics: Up to 53% higher attack success than SOTA baselines.
notes: ACM SenSys 2026.

name: TouchSafeBench (collision grounding for HRC)
modality: Habitat 3.0 co-presence episodes with multi-view RGB-D, trajectory maps and camera metadata; VLM classifies current safety state and imminent collision; Macro-F1 against simulator contact labels.
what_it_measures: Whether VLMs can ground physical contact risk between humans and robots from visual input.
size: 2,940 simulated episodes; 3 VLMs x 9 visual representations.
reported_metrics: Best average Macro-F1 below 50%.
cost_evidence: Labels from simulator physics (no human labelling cost).
validity_evidence: Ground truth is simulator contact, not human judgement.

name: No Free Checker (survey of verifiers)
modality: Survey of ~150 verifiers for robot policies (success detectors, reward models, runtime monitors, safety filters, temporal-logic specs) along credibility vs availability (cost, earliness, frequency of verdict).
what_it_measures: Frames verifier choice as a credibility-vs-availability trade-off; catalogues how verifiers are validated (human agreement, downstream policy performance, reward-hacking resilience).
reported_metrics: Credibility falls as availability rises across the four families.
cost_evidence: Explicitly treats verdict cost as a first-class axis.
validity_evidence: Lists validation practices but no numbers.
notes: Directly relevant framing for a VOI paper.

name: REBAR (ethical benchmark for autonomy readiness)
modality: LLM-generated test instances in a photorealistic simulator; neuro-symbolic LLM approach; metrics mapped to an Autonomy Readiness Level rubric.
what_it_measures: Ethical/safety readiness of autonomous systems via at-scale generated scenarios.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.
notes: WOROBET 2026 workshop; details thin.

name: Semantic Denial of Service in LLM-controlled robots
modality: Short (1-5 token) safety-plausible audio phrases injected to halt robot operation without jailbreaking; 4 VLMs, 7 prompt-level defenses, 3 deployment modes; Disruption Success Rate.
what_it_measures: Availability attacks that exploit safety refusals (false-alarm exploitation).
reported_metrics: Prompt-only defenses trade attack suppression against legitimate safety responses.

name: SafetyALFRED
modality: ALFRED augmented with hazards; MLLMs tested on disembodied hazard-recognition QA and on embodied planning that must mitigate the hazard; 11 models (Qwen, Gemma, Gemini).
what_it_measures: Gap between recognising a hazard in QA and mitigating it in embodied planning.
reported_metrics: Mitigation success rates low relative to QA recognition.
notes: ACL 2026 Findings.

name: SENTINEL
modality: Temporal-logic safety specs checked at three levels: semantic interpretation, plan generation and physical execution (VirtualHome, AI2-THOR); execution trajectories merged into computation trees.
what_it_measures: Formal multi-level safety verification of foundation-model embodied agents.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.
notes: v3 July 2026.

name: EmbodyGuard (Subtle Risks, Critical Failures)
modality: LLM-generated text scenarios; Command Refusal Test and Plan Safety Test decomposed into goal interpretation, transition modelling and action sequencing; 13 LLMs.
what_it_measures: Whether LLM planners anticipate subtle situational physical risks, beyond refusing overt commands.
reported_metrics: Models refuse overt commands but fail subtle situational risks (numbers not in abstract).

name: Defining and Evaluating Physical Safety for LLMs (drones)
modality: LLM generates drone control code for prompts spanning human-targeted, object-targeted, infrastructure and regulatory risks; evaluates refusal and unsafe code generation; ICL/CoT mitigations.
what_it_measures: Trade-off between code-generation capability and physical safety in LLM drone control.
reported_metrics: Larger models safer; ICL/CoT help but not for unintentional attacks.
notes: Communications of the ACM 2026.

name: PhysicalJailbreakBench-2K / PRISM
modality: Hidden-state probing of open LLMs on SafeAgentBench-style tasks; 2,000 comparison rows contrasting textual-safe vs physically unsafe outputs; logistic probe over hidden states.
what_it_measures: Whether physical-harm risk is separable from textual jailbreak risk in model internals.
size: 2,000 rows from a 10,000-row pool; Qwen2.5 3B-32B, Phi-3.5, SmolLM2.
reported_metrics: 86.2-87.7% accuracy on SafeAgentBench with 11.7-13.7% false positives; PRISM AUC 0.718 vs 0.398 control.

name: CORE (contextual safety reasoning and grounding)
modality: VLM continuously infers context-dependent safety rules from images, grounds them spatially, and enforces safe sets with control barrier functions; simulation and real-world experiments in unseen environments.
what_it_measures: Runtime enforcement of semantically derived safety constraints on a real robot.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.

name: SafeManip
modality: LTLf temporal safety properties across 8 categories monitored on VLA rollouts in RoboCasa365; 6 VLAs x 50 household tasks.
what_it_measures: Temporal safety compliance of VLA policies independent of success.
reported_metrics: Many successful rollouts remain unsafe (numbers not in abstract).

name: SIMMER
modality: Human-curated symbolic kitchen world model (77 actions, 262 objects, ~46,800 interactions) with a state-machine executor that flags precondition violations, latent hazards and irreversible failures in LLM plans.
what_it_measures: Latent (delayed) failures in LLM executable plans.
reported_metrics: At most 17% error-free plans for frontier models; up to 56% contain latent failures; counterfactual foresight cuts latent failures up to 72%.
notes: COLM 2026.

name: HomeGuard
modality: VLM safeguard with context-guided CoT (perception anchoring then semantic judgement) trained by RFT with process rewards on a curated grounding dataset; risk match rate and over-safety measured.
what_it_measures: Contextual risk identification for household tasks with reduced over-refusal.
reported_metrics: >30% risk-match improvement over baselines; reduced over-safety.
notes: Same group as IS-Bench.

name: RVSG (VLM-based testing of industrial AMRs)
org: Simula Research Laboratory / Mondragon / PAL Robotics
modality: VLM generates diverse human behaviours that violate functional and safety requirements to test a PAL Robotics AMR in simulation; measures requirement violations and behaviour variability.
what_it_measures: Scenario generation for safety testing of industrial mobile robots.
reported_metrics: More requirement-violating scenarios and behaviour variability than baselines.
notes: Industrial partner involvement; still simulation only.

name: Semantically Safe Robot Manipulation
modality: 3D semantic map + LLM inference of semantically unsafe conditions mapped to control-barrier-certified constraints; real kitchen experiments with teleoperation and diffusion policies.
what_it_measures: Runtime semantic safety filtering beyond geometric collision avoidance.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.

name: MADRA / SafeAware-VH
modality: Multiple LLM agents debate instruction safety with consensus voting; evaluated on AI2-THOR, VirtualHome and a new SafeAware-VH set of 800 annotated instructions; rejection and false-rejection rates.
what_it_measures: Training-free risk-aware planning with low false rejection.
reported_metrics: >90% rejection of unsafe tasks with low false rejection.

name: How Long Until Your Robot Ignores You? (humanoid LLM orchestrator benchmark)
org: Fraunhofer IPA (assumed from CBS venue; not verified)
modality: Long multi-turn sessions (100 turns) with an LLM orchestrating a Unitree G1 humanoid; text prompting, simulated sensor-actuator loops and (ongoing) physical validation; 4-level compliance taxonomy (correct, over-, under-compliance, violation).
what_it_measures: Drift of LLM orchestrator safety compliance over long human-humanoid sessions.
reported_metrics: Claude and Gemini zero violations; GPT-4o-mini up to 13 per session; context management cuts issues 42-57%.
notes: CBS 2026. Org unverified.

name: LLM safety for robotic health attendant control
modality: 270 harmful instructions grounded in AMA medical-ethics principles sent to 72 LLMs in a Robotic Health Attendant simulation; violation rate.
what_it_measures: Refusal of ethically prohibited instructions by LLMs controlling a care robot.
reported_metrics: Mean violation 54.4%; proprietary median 23.7% vs open-weight 72.8%.
notes: Widest model coverage (72 LLMs) in the catalogue.

name: DAERT (diversity-aware embodied red teaming)
modality: Uniform policy generates varied instructions; failures measured by execution in a physics simulator on pi0 and OpenVLA.
what_it_measures: Linguistic fragility of VLAs.
reported_metrics: Average success 93.33% -> 5.85%.
notes: safety_focus false: task-success robustness.

name: ICAT (incident-case-grounded adaptive testing of world models)
modality: Structured risk memories built from real incident reports and safety manuals are retrieved to compose risk cases with causal chains and severity labels; video world models are tested on whether generated futures show the hazard mechanism and severity.
what_it_measures: Physical-risk fidelity of generative world models used as neural simulators.
reported_metrics: Mainstream world models miss mechanisms/triggers and miscalibrate severity.
validity_evidence: Grounded in real incident reports; no quantitative human agreement.
notes: Relevant to validity of level-3/5 generative evaluations.

name: ANNIE / ANNIEBench
modality: Task-aware attack leader decomposes long-horizon goals into frame-level perturbations of embodied AI models; taxonomy of violations (critical, dangerous, risky) by separation distance, velocity, collision boundary; physical robot validation.
what_it_measures: Attack success in inducing physically unsafe behaviour of embodied models.
reported_metrics: Attack success >50% across all safety categories.
validity_evidence: Physical-constraint-based violation taxonomy; no human study.

name: RoboSafe
modality: Executable predicate-based safety logic with backward reflective and forward predictive reasoning; evaluated on multiple agents and real robotic arms; risk occurrence reduction.
what_it_measures: Runtime safeguarding of embodied agents.
reported_metrics: -36.8% risk occurrence vs leading baselines with near-original task performance.

name: Safety in Embodied AI: survey of risks, attacks, defenses
modality: Survey of >500 papers across perception, cognition, planning, action and interaction.
what_it_measures: Consolidates attack/defense literature; highlights fragile multimodal fusion and planning instability under jailbreaks.
reported_metrics: n/a
notes: Author list truncated (41 authors).

name: JailWAM
modality: Adversarial instructions against world action models (LingBot-VA) in RoboTwin; dual-path verification (risk screening + simulation) with a three-level risk discriminator.
what_it_measures: Jailbreak success against world-action robot models.
reported_metrics: 84.2% attack success on LingBot-VA.

name: Hijacking Robots with a Piece of Paper (physical prompt injection)
org: Singapore University of Technology and Design
modality: Printed adversarial text (signage, task redefinition, authority impersonation, conflict injection) placed in the visual field of VLM-controlled robots; 5,670 trials across 20 prompts, 3 command formulations and 3 scene layouts; attack success rate and acknowledgement rate.
what_it_measures: Susceptibility of VLM robot controllers to visual text injection and the efficacy of mitigations.
reported_metrics: ASR 27.0% (GPT-4o), 29.4% (Gemini), 5.0% (Qwen3-VL); attacks acknowledged 99.9% of the time; defenses 75-100% effective.
notes: Whether trials ran on physical robots is unclear; physical scene layouts suggest at least level 1, possibly 7.

name: SHAWSHANK-BENCH (indirect environmental jailbreaks)
modality: Malicious instructions embedded in the environment rather than the prompt; auto-generated benchmark of task-scene combinations; six VLMs; compared to eleven attack methods.
what_it_measures: Vulnerability of embodied VLM agents to environment-borne injections.
reported_metrics: Outperforms 11 existing methods; defenses only partially mitigate.
notes: Environment type not stated; level 4 assumed.

name: WorldEval (world model as real-world policy evaluator)
modality: Policy2Vec turns a video generation model into a latent-action-following world simulator; policy performance in generated rollouts compared with real-world scenarios; also used as a safety detector for dangerous actions.
what_it_measures: Whether a video world model ranks real robot policies correctly and flags dangerous actions before deployment.
reported_metrics: Strong correlation with real-world performance claimed; outperforms real-to-sim approaches.
cost_evidence: Motivated by cost of real evaluation; no numbers.
validity_evidence: Correlation with real evaluation claimed but coefficient not in abstract.
notes: Companion evidence to geminirobotics2025veo.

name: SafeGate (pre-execution safety gate)
modality: Neurosymbolic extraction of safety properties from commands, task safety contracts (invariants, guards, aborts) and Z3 SMT checks before execution; 230 benchmark tasks, 30 AI2-THOR scenarios, real-robot experiments.
what_it_measures: Rejection of defective/unsafe commands before execution with high benign acceptance.
reported_metrics: Significantly reduced acceptance of defective commands; high benign acceptance (numbers not in abstract).
notes: Follow-up to SafePlan.

name: BeSafe-Bench
modality: Functional environments across Web, Mobile, Embodied VLM and Embodied VLA domains with tasks augmented by nine risk categories; hybrid rule-based checks plus LLM-as-a-judge; 13 agents.
what_it_measures: Behavioural safety of situated agents while completing tasks.
reported_metrics: Best agent completes <40% of tasks while fully adhering to safety constraints.
notes: Embodied portion only partially described.

name: MulRobBench (UAV agents)
modality: Real UAV multimodal observations plus protocol-level security-policy constraints; VLA UAV agents scored on semantic protocol decisions and strict structural diagnostics (policy compliance, unsafe actions, formatting).
what_it_measures: Safe, policy-compliant decision-making of multimodal UAV agents.
reported_metrics: Best semantic score 0.5141; best strict dimension accuracy 0.1599.
notes: Aerial rather than manipulation; included for real-data-replay coverage.
